belief_statement: Preliminary evidence indicates that component high reversed specular has inconsistent effects on appearance perceived surface. The evidence base (4 findings, 2 studies) is growing but not yet conclusive.

latent_variables.name: Mechanism selection
latent_variables.rationale: Multiple mechanisms are implicated (Psychophysics / Perception, Multisensory Integration). A latent variable may determine which pathway is activated.

latent_variables.name: Dose and duration
latent_variables.rationale: Most studies measure presence/absence of component high reversed specular, not dose-response curves. Duration and intensity likely matter.
latent_variables.suggested_measure: Parametric variation of intensity and exposure duration

research_needs.question: Does the effect of component high reversed specular on appearance perceived surface replicate in a pre-registered RCT?
research_needs.rationale: Current confidence is moderate. A well-powered pre-registered replication would most efficiently resolve the status of this belief.

research_needs.question: Which mechanism best explains component high reversed specular → appearance perceived surface?
research_needs.rationale: 2 candidate mechanisms exist. Process tracing would identify the active pathway.

research_needs.question: What is the dose-response curve for component high reversed specular effects on appearance perceived surface?
research_needs.rationale: Dose-response data enables design guidelines with specific thresholds.
